title: priority-backoff-reservation-gateway-and-utilization-telemetry
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds a priority-aware reservation gateway to improve graceful backoff for low-priority tenants and new utilization telemetry fields for per-tenant headroom reporting. No customer-facing API changes.
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleets need a lightweight admission/ reservation layer that can apply priority-aware backoff without perturbing global autoscaler heuristics. This PR introduces a Reservation Gateway that mediates incoming reservation requests, applies configurable priority backoff curves, and exposes per-tenant headroom/utilization telemetry for better downstream SLO decisions. Goals: 1) Surface a low-latency decision path for reservation/admission that can immediately decline or soft-backoff low-priority requests. 2) Emit per-tenant headroom and queued-reservation metrics to aid autoscaler and SRE. 3) Keep changes backward-compatible with existing reservation semantics and fall back to current allocator when disabled. High-level changes: implemented a gateway component (pkg/autoscaler/gateway.go) which intercepts ReservationCreate calls, evaluates tenant priority and recent-utilization fingerprints, and applies a tunable exponential backoff function; added an in-memory reservation cache with soft-lease semantics (pkg/autoscaler/reservation_store.go) to avoid hot-path DB calls; introduced a telemetry shim (pkg/telemetry/util_reporter.go) that normalizes headroom and short-window utilization into new metrics (redwood.reservation.headroom_pct, redwood.reservation.smr_util_p50, redwood.reservation.queued_count); added Helm flags and a feature gate to enable the gateway per-cluster (cmd/infra/deploy/helm/templates/gateway.yaml); updated docs and runbook (docs/ops/dedicated-fleet.md) with configuration examples and recommended thresholds; added unit and integration tests (tests/autoscaler/gateway_test.go, tests/telemetry/reporting_integration_test.go). Backwards compatibility & safety: feature is behind a cluster-level feature flag and defaults to disabled. Gateway consults the existing reservation store and will forward to the canonical allocator for any tenant marked as "legacy-managed." Feature rollout plan: 1) Canary enable in dev clusters for 48h and monitor headroom metrics and queued reservation delta. 2) Gradual rollout to regional fleets with conservative backoff curve. 3) If increase in failed admissions or unexpected throttling observed, revert via helm flag. Checklist: [x] Gateway core logic implemented [x] Telemetry metrics exposed and documented [x] Helm config and feature flag [x] Unit/integration tests [x] Runbook & rollout notes added [x] Performance microbenchmark shows <1ms median additional latency on warm path (measured in perf-lab). Related Linear/Jira: ENG-3124 (priority backoff design), ENG-3187 (telemetry schema), SUP-789 (customer incident motivating soft-decline).
commits_summary: 4 commits: 1) gateway: initial pass with decision engine and config plumbing; 2) reservation_store: soft-lease cache and eviction policy; 3) telemetry: new normalized headroom metrics and exporter; 4) ops: helm flags, docs and tests. Each commit includes unit tests and basic bench harness for warm-path latency.
